title: Games capped at 60 FPS with overall lag on Nothing Phone (2a), despite 120Hz display
body: ### Tested versions I believe this issue is present on all Godot versions, though I have not tested every release individually to confirm. ### System information Godot v4.7.2.stable - Windows 10.0 (build 22631) - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6600 - AMD Ryzen 7 5800XT 8-Core Processor (16 Threads) ### Issue description On the Nothing Phone (2a), most games are locked to a maximum of 60 FPS and never reach the phone's native 120Hz refresh rate, even in titles that support higher frame rates. Beyond the cap itself, gameplay also feels generally laggy/stuttery rather than just "smooth but capped at 60." #### Expected Behavior Supported games should be able to run up to 120 FPS on the 120Hz panel, with smooth, consistent frame pacing. #### Actual Behavior FPS is capped at 60 max, and overall performance feels laggy — inconsistent frame times, not just a lower ceiling. #### Environment - Device: Nothing Phone (2a) - Nothing OS version: 4.1 - Android version: 16 - Games affected: every More specs: #### Attempted Workarounds - Toggling Developer Options > "Disable default frame rate for game" and "Force peak refresh rate" — inconsistent results - Third-party overlay apps (e.g. Assistive Touch) reported by some community members to unlock 120 FPS — unreliable, breaks on OS updates - Clearing cache / reinstalling games — no effect - Factory reset — not a reasonable fix for a systemic issue #### Additional Context This has been discussed repeatedly in the Nothing Community forum across OS versions (2.5.x, 2.6, and into OS 4.0 betas), suggesting it isn't tied to one release but a persistent frame-rate governor/game-detection issue. Users report it affects many popular titles, not isolated apps. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new Godot project (or use any existing project). 2. Export the project to Android using the default export preset, with no custom frame rate settings changed. 3. Install and run the exported APK on a Nothing Phone (2a) with the display refresh rate set to 120Hz. 4. Observe that the game is capped at 60 FPS and does not reach 120 FPS, with overall performance feeling laggy/stuttery.
